    Export for Roblox

    Get a Studio-ready head file with your makeup assigned. No Blender or Maya needed.

    File
    Texture size
    What you get, and how to bring it into Studio
    • LookName.gltf: Roblox's reference makeup head with your textures already assigned to TransferTexture_Face_01, _Eyes_01 and _Lips_01.
    • textures/: colour (ALB, with transparency), roughness (RGH), metalness (MET) and normal (NOR) PNGs for each region.
    • uv-guide.png and preview.png for reference.

    In Roblox Studio, open the Makeup reference place or your own, then use the 3D Importer on LookName.gltf. Studio reads the TransferTexture names and generates the makeup Decal objects under the imported model. Drag those Decals into a character's Makeup folder, and the eyebrow and eyelash parts into its Accessories folder.

    How Vanity works

    Roblox makeup is three transparent textures that share the head's UV layout: Face (base, blush, contour, face paint), Eyes (shadow, liner) and Lips. Every layer belongs to one of them, and on export each region's layers are flattened into its own texture set.

    A Full face layer lets you paint across all three at once. On export, its lip area goes to Lips, its eye area to Eyes and the rest to Face, so a full look can be painted in one pass. The tinted overlay shows where the cuts fall, and Split into regions does the same cut in the editor.

    Paint on the flat texture or straight onto the head. The finish (roughness and metalness) is set per layer, so put gloss and matte on separate layers.

    B / A / S / U / E / T / IBrush, airbrush, blend, smudge, eraser, stamp, eyedropper
    [ and ]Smaller / larger brush
    Shift + clickStraight line from the last point
    Alt (hold)Eyedropper
    Space + drag, wheelPan and zoom the texture
    Right-drag or Shift-drag on headTurn the head
    Project (on the head view)Projection painting: strokes on the head are projected from your view, like a decal, instead of following the texture
    M / RToggle mirror / clip to region
    Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+ZUndo, redo
